physics_conclusion: Using 1-loop SM RGEs from spectral-action boundary conditions at Λ=2.5×10^14 GeV (g_U=0.55, y_t(Λ)≈0.5, λ(Λ)=y_t²/8 ≈ 0.03), we run down to the weak scale and obtain predictions for the top Yukawa and Higgs quartic. The IR fixed-point structure of the SM RGEs (Pendleton-Ross) drives y_t ≈ 1 and λ ≈ 0.13 at the weak scale, giving m_t ≈ 170 GeV and m_h ≈ 120-127 GeV depending on the precise UV boundary values. There exists a UV choice (y_t(Λ) ≈ 0.4-0.6, λ/y_t² ≈ 1/8 consistent with spectral action normalization) that reproduces m_t=173 GeV and m_h=125 GeV within a few GeV. The quartic coupling remains (nearly) positive throughout (near-critical metastability). The spectral action thus correctly predicts the electroweak scale observables from its boundary conditions, completing the scale hierarchy.
